//: Copy a block into providers.json and edit it. A PROVIDER is a connection; the models it serves nest under it, and each is addressed as <provider>/<model>. Nothing is seeded pointing anywhere, because a url that is right on one machine is wrong on the next.

local.//: A local llama.cpp / llama-server. No api key needed.
local.//2: Provider-level values are defaults for every model below; a model may override any of them.

small.//: Same endpoint, different model, its own limits. This is the case a flat one-entry-per-model file could not express.

hosted.//: A hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Use api_key_env, never api_key, unless this file is outside version control and readable only by you.

auto.//: With "discover": true the backend lists its own models -- no "models" object needed (static entries beside it still work, and a model's own window always wins over the provider default). The list is fetched lazily, never written back to this file, and /providers refresh re-fetches it on demand. Works with any OpenAI-shaped backend provider-openai covers: llama.cpp, vLLM, OpenRouter.

anthropic.//: The Anthropic Messages API. url is WITHOUT a /v1 suffix -- unlike the openai backend's convention, provider-anthropic appends /v1/messages itself. max_tokens is REQUIRED (not optional the way OpenAI treats it): set it here or per-model below, or every request fails.
anthropic.//2: cache_ttl is "5m" (the default; omit it) or "1h" -- see ARCHITECTURE.md's prompt-caching notes on when the 1h write premium pays for itself.

claude-opus-5.//: The model KEY is sent on the wire verbatim as the request's "model" field -- unlike the provider name, it is NOT yours to choose; it must be the backend's real model id. A key MAY contain '/' (split at the first one), so ids like "anthropic/claude-opus-5" are expressible -- see the openrouter block below.

openrouter.//: OpenRouter is an ordinary openai-backend endpoint; its model ids are vendor/model, and a static model key may carry that '/' (the full ref is then three segments: openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5). Or set "discover": true and drop "models" entirely -- OpenRouter's catalog supplies ids and context windows.
openrouter.//app: Set "openrouter_app_id": true to opt this entry's usage into OpenRouter app attribution: every request (chat and model discovery) carries the project's identity (X-Title: minimal, HTTP-Referer: the project's GitHub URL). An explicit "headers" entry of the same name wins.
openrouter.//2: Every request (turns, subagents, compaction) carries the harness session id as a top-level "session_id" by default. OpenRouter uses it as its sticky-routing key -- the whole session lands on the provider endpoint whose prompt cache is warm, and the requests group in the Logs "Sessions" view. A backend that rejects unknown body fields opts out with "parameters": { "session_id": false }; a string value passes through verbatim as a static routing key. provider-anthropic sends the same value as the x-session-id header instead.

anthropic/claude-opus-5.//: parameters are spread verbatim into the request body, so OpenRouter's provider-routing field passes through untouched: this pins the model to those upstream providers (other keys: ignore, order, allow_fallbacks).

models.//variants: "variants" turns one model into several addressable effort variants: <model>@<name>. The LIST form names effort levels (known: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, minimal, none) and derives the wire parameters per backend -- anthropic entries get thinking:{type:enabled,budget_tokens:N} with a per-name budget (clamped to fit max_tokens), openai-shape entries get reasoning_effort. The MAP form (see below) writes the request fields explicitly instead. Variant refs appear in /model and --model like any model; the @suffix is never sent on the wire.

z-ai/glm-5.3-flash.//2: The list form: three one-word variants. Wire ids stay 'z-ai/glm-5.3-flash'.

z-ai/glm-5.3-flash2.//3: The map form (opencode-style passthrough): a named variant body -- parameters verbatim, plus optional variant-scoped max_tokens / context_window_tokens. Unknown keys inside a body are a parse error.

models.//4: A provider-level "variants" (either form) applies to EVERY model under the entry -- for a "discover": true entry it IS the autodiscovery recipe: models whose catalog advertises reasoning efforts get exactly these variants. With no recipe, discovery AUTODETECTS: every model that advertises an effort ladder gets its own ladder verbatim (glm-5.3-flash's supported_efforts [max,high,low] becomes @max, @high, @low with zero config); a model advertising no ladder gets none.

//3: Then point settings.json at one of them: "default_model": "local/qwen4". An agent preset may name its own with `model: local/small`, and --model or /model overrides both.
